comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Minor but should be fixed in any clean write-up. The displayed identity in the proof of Cor 2.7 reads
  |v*|^2 = |a+b|^2 = |a^*|^2 + 2(a.b) + |b^*|^2,
but there are no starred objects a^*, b^*; the terms are simply |a|^2 and |b|^2. The logic ('|a|^2 >= |v*|^2 and |b|^2 > 0 => a.b < 0') is correct; only the notation is wrong.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
Investigated the displayed identity in the proof of Corollary 2.7 (labeled cor:apex). The current solution.tex does NOT contain the reported typo: there are no occurrences of a^*, b^*, |a^*|^2, or |b^*|^2 anywhere in the file (verified by grep over the raw LaTeX). The display already reads correctly via the 
orm macro:

  |v^*|^2 = |a+b|^2 = |a|^2 + 2(a.b) + |b|^2 > |v^*|^2 + 2(a.b),

i.e. 
orm{v^\ast} = 
orm{a+b} = 
orm a + 2(a\cdot b) + 
orm b > 
orm{v^\ast} + 2(a\cdot b). Here 
orm a = |a|^2 and 
orm b = |b|^2 (the macro is 
orm[1]{|#1|^2}); the only starred objects in the proof are the genuinely-defined dual basis element v^* (and v_i^* elsewhere). The logic is exactly as the critic notes and is correct: a.v != 0 gives |a|^2 >= |v^*|^2 (Lemma apex), and b != 0 gives |b|^2 > 0 by positive-definiteness, so the identity forces 2(a.b) < 0, hence v^* is irreducible.

Conclusion: the notational typo flagged in this issue is not present in the current write-up (it was presumably fixed in an earlier revision or filed against an older draft). No change to the mathematics is needed; the proof of Cor 2.7 is clean and correct. Marking resolved.
